The minimum-risk three-grade report puts F and I in the same grade despite strong posterior evidence for F above I.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **F above I.** Probability is above .999; across 175,099 reports stating it, best risk is .0641 (optimum .0638).
- **I above F.** Requiring the reverse direction raises minimum risk to .112.
- **The tertiles state it.** Tertile cuts state 48 pairs at risk .0823, stating F above I in three grades.
- **The higher-cost optimum.** At τ = .45, the optimum states F above I at risk .143.

<details>
<summary>Family restrictions and scope notes</summary>

Requiring F above I can change comparisons involving other schools, so the browser searches the three-grade family again with that direction required. In Method, a four-grade dynamic-programming search along the posterior-mean order admits reports that the three-grade search excludes while excluding non-monotone groupings; both use the same posterior, τ, and weight, so their risks are directly comparable. A shared grade leaves relative chronic absence unstated. This twelve-school teaching subset is conditional on a statewide prior fitted to 5,834 eligible schools (prior-estimation uncertainty is not propagated). California's Dashboard colors, school quality, causal effects, and statewide calibration require evidence beyond this subset. Related: [Reasons for a withheld comparison](../criteria/why-withheld.qmd) · [The error–disclosure frontier](../grades/frontier.qmd).

</details>

Data: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26, adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (`pr_case_cde`); <https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp>; not relicensed, provided as is; No CDE endorsement is implied.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## In postrank

This call reads the probability of F above I from the original case-study input.

```r
library(postrank)
e <- postrank_pairwise(pr_case_cde$input)$e
1 - e[6, 9, 1]
```
:::
